reason: create_stream_state initializes two mutexes. remove_stream_state destroys both; shutdown_stream_state_manager destroys only mutex before freeing. Consolidating final disposal removes divergent resource lifecycle paths.

ownership.allocation: create_stream_state owns calloc and both pthread_mutex_init calls; on second init failure destroys first and frees
ownership.registry: stream_states stores pointers under states_mutex; removal detaches same slot under that lock
ownership.borrowing: get_stream_state_by_name returns borrowed pointer; existing caller/ref lifecycle is not changed
ownership.final_disposal: new private helper destroys mutex and state_mutex then frees, called only after existing stop/quiescence path
ownership.thread_affinity: no new thread; existing removal/shutdown caller performs disposal
ownership.locks: states_mutex held for final disposal; state->mutex and state_mutex must be unlocked and unused; helper acquires no locks
ownership.callbacks: no callback registration or disable ordering change
ownership.cancellation_shutdown: existing stop and shutdown ordering preserved; main stops stream manager and adapter first
ownership.scope_limit: No repair of unrelated concurrent borrowed-pointer lifetime or state-transition policy is claimed.

behavior_invariants: No state layout, public signature, persistence or wire change
Both initialized per-state mutexes destroyed exactly once on removal and global shutdown
Refused removal with extra references destroys neither mutex
Repeated global shutdown performs no additional per-state destroy
Repeated create/remove/shutdown cycles preserve current registry and reference behavior
physical_qualification: deferred by user; no performance claim
